audit.why: 52.73% over 550 games matches a chart that gives Camille levels 1-5 and the first item, marks 6 as Skill because both ults arrive, and hands K'Sante the two-item stage. The stage split is consistent with the number and with All Out being his real spike, so I left every side and rating alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The early spikes are built on 'three stacked Q charges' and dives are keyed to 'his W-charge and E-dash cooldown windows' with no numbers. Ntofo Strikes is a 3.5s flat cooldown that shockwaves at TWO stacks, so there is no three-charge window to race; Path Maker is 14s and Footwork 10s, and those are the cooldowns your dive is actually keyed to.
audit.why: Riot, Ntofo Strikes: 'On hit, grants a stack of Ntofo Strikes. At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in.' Cooldowns from champ-data/_kits/ksante.json: Q 3.5s flat, W 14/13/12/11/10s, E 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, spikes[2].text, early, whys[2] and whys[5] now use two stacks and carry Path Maker's 14s / Footwork's 10s as the dive window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interaction errors and two omissions. (1) His Q was called a knock-up on the third hit; it is a PULL at two stacks - the difference matters because a pull drags you in rather than launching you, so it feeds his follow-up instead of interrupting it. (2) Footwork (E) is only ever called 'his E-dash'; it also shields him, which is precisely what eats your Q-recast burst - force it out first. (3) All Out heals him, and there is no Grievous Wounds call anywhere on the page. Also, Path Maker stuns as well as knocking back, and stops doing either while he is All Out. Camille's Hookshot is called a stun throughout; Riot's text says knock-up.
audit.why: Riot: Ntofo Strikes - 'At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in.' Footwork - 'K'Sante dashes and gains a shield.' Path Maker - 'charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes, knocking back and stunning enemies. When All Out, deals increased damage and no longer knocks back or stuns.' All Out - 'gaining increased damage, healing, and transformed abilities.' _missing-interactions.json flags shield-absorbs-burst, needs-antiheal and autoreset-burst-tell for this pairing.
audit.corrected: early, mid, whys[2], wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1] now say pull-at-two-stacks, name Footwork's shield as the thing to bait, and late buys anti-heal against All Out.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere, in a matchup the page itself says flips because he becomes 'a lifesteal fighter'.
audit.why: All Out grants healing on top of the lifesteal, and it is the stated reason the two-item stage is his. Grievous Wounds bought before that stage is the itemisation answer the page never gave.
audit.corrected: late now names the Grievous Wounds timing against All Out.

edits.before: Second point plus your W slash-heal online: walk up and short-trade — your Q re-cast true damage out-DPSes him before he has armor stacked or three Q charges for the knock-up.
edits.after: Second point plus your W slash-heal online: walk up and short-trade — your Q re-cast true damage out-DPSes him before he has armor stacked or two Ntofo Strikes stacks for the pull.

edits.before: Your bruiser/lethality item plus boots is your peak: dive him on his W-charge and E-dash cooldown windows and snowball before his tank items come online.
edits.after: Your bruiser/lethality item plus boots is your peak: dive when Path Maker (W, 14s) and Footwork (E, 10s) are both down and snowball before his tank items come online.

edits.before: Level 1 is even-ish since neither of you has a real all-in, so last-hit and don't waste a Q he can simply walk through with W's damage reduction. From Level 2 you take over: walk up and short-trade with your Q re-cast for the true-damage second hit while your W outer-cone slash heals you off him. His Q only knocks up on the third stacked hit and his body is squishy before tank items, so quick trades are all yours — just respect that his W charge gives damage reduction and then a knock-back dash, so don't dump everything into it.
edits.after: Level 1 is even-ish since neither of you has a real all-in, so last-hit and don't waste a Q he can walk through with Path Maker's damage reduction. From Level 2 you take over: short-trade with your Q re-cast for the true-damage second hit while your W outer-cone slash heals you off him. Ntofo Strikes is a 3.5s cooldown that shockwaves and PULLS you in at two stacks, so break contact after one. Bait Footwork (E, 10s) too — the shield on that dash is what eats your burst if you commit into it.

edits.before: This is your kill window. Levels 3-5 you out-trade him cleanly, and at 6 your Hextech Ultimatum arenas him into a 1v1 where his R knock-back, peel and CC utility are wasted while your W melts his percent-HP bulk. The whole fight is his W: the channel reduces the damage he takes and then dashes him with a knock-back, so bait it with an early Q or a faked E-dash before you commit your real E-Q stun-burst. Once his W and Q charges are spent he has no tool to peel himself out of your arena.
edits.after: This is your kill window. Levels 3-5 you out-trade him cleanly, and at 6 your Hextech Ultimatum arenas him into a 1v1 where his peel and CC utility are wasted while your W melts his percent-HP bulk. The whole fight is his W: Path Maker charges with damage reduction, then dashes with a knock-back and a stun, so bait it with an early Q or a faked E-dash. Bait Footwork's shield too. Once W, the shield and his Ntofo stacks are spent he has nothing left to peel himself out of your arena.

edits.before: Be honest: K'Sante is a hard scaler and the lane flips around two tank items. His R (All Out) breaks his tank stance — trading raw resists for range, attack damage and lifesteal — so he becomes a fast, sustained fighter who survives your full combo and out-duels you in the all-in your W used to win. Close this out in the early-to-mid window: get a lead, take plates and turret, then splitpush or use R to peel a fed K'Sante off your carries and isolate a squishier target rather than dueling him straight up.
edits.after: Be honest: K'Sante is a hard scaler and the lane flips around two tank items. All Out (R) breaks his tank stance — trading raw resists for range, damage and healing — so he becomes a fast, sustained fighter who survives your full combo and out-duels you in the all-in your W used to win. Buy Grievous Wounds before that stage arrives or the heal alone beats you. Close this out early: get a lead, take plates and turret, then splitpush or use R to peel him off your carries and isolate a squishier target rather than dueling him straight up.

edits.before: Hookshot (E) unlocks your wall-dash stun and attack-speed burst. Only take a wall trade when K'Sante's All Out is down, then peel out on the bonus move speed before he answers. Camille is favoured here.
edits.after: Hookshot (E) unlocks your wall-dash knock-up and attack-speed burst. Only take a wall trade when K'Sante's All Out is down, then peel out on the bonus move speed before he answers. Camille is favoured here.

edits.before: Good trade: Lead with the W outer edge as K'Sante steps to last-hit, weave the empowered Q2 true damage, then peel out on your bonus move speed before the fight goes long. Great trade: K'Sante uses or whiffs All Out: instantly E off a wall for the stun and attack-speed surge, Q-recast for the true-damage second hit, W to heal, and R to isolate him if he tries to run. Bad trade: Burning Hookshot (E) aggressively, missing the stun, and getting stuck in a drawn-out melee grind while your E and shield are down. That is how Camille loses a winning lane.

edits.before: Your E-stun off a wall into the empowered Q2 is a premium gank setup — ping your jungler when E is up and K'Sante's escape is down. You are most vulnerable right after you E in with it on cooldown, so ward the river bush before you dive.

notes: The 'third stacked Q knock-up' was wrong in five places: Ntofo Strikes shockwaves at TWO stacks and PULLS rather than knocking up, on a 3.5s flat cooldown - which also means the page's advice to race him before he 'stacks three Q charges' described a window that does not exist. Footwork's shield was the biggest omission: the page kept calling it 'his E-dash' while the shield is exactly what absorbs the Q-recast burst it tells you to commit. I deliberately did NOT write anything about whether All Out's wall-launching knock-back can remove Camille from The Hextech Ultimatum's anchored area - Riot's text says it launches the target through any wall in their path, but nothing in either kit file settles the interaction with her ult, and a player would bet the fight on that answer. Logged as unverified.
